_comment: One general manager's day, on a phone. Times are the planned timeline in seconds; model waits stretch it and --compress-waits squeezes them back. Captions are the narration: read them aloud in the voice-over, or keep them as subtitles.

steps.say: 07:00 — the day starts with one screen: what to decide today.
RED. Eight overdue. Assembly 39% below its normal range for six days. Three decisions.
Each card is one decision with one button. Nothing here was asked for: the discovery tool found it.
09:40 — on the floor. “How is the TrendCart order doing?”

type.text: How is the TrendCart order doing?

steps.say: TrendCart has six orders, so it asks instead of guessing.
Now it knows which order: ORD-005, 500 scarves, at knitting, due 20 April, idle 8 days.
The reason comes from the data, and every number opens the rows behind it.
11:15 — “A customer wants 800 hoodies by the 25th. Can we take it?”

type.text: Can we take 800 hoodies by the 25th?

steps.say: It asks the one thing that changes the answer: ready at the factory, or delivered?
An estimate with its assumptions: the queue's finish date, the on-time chance, the bottleneck stage. Not a yes.

type.text: What if packing loses a day?

steps.say: What-ifs re-run the same tool with one assumption changed.
14:30 — assembly has not recovered. “Chase it up.”

type.text: Draft a chase-up to the assembly department: output has been below range for 6 days. Ask what changed and when it will recover.

steps.say: A draft, addressed to the department, with the facts filled in. Nothing is sent yet.
Preview first. Sending needs the manager's confirmation, and it is logged.
Sent, and recorded in the activity log with who, when and what.
17:00 — “Remind me tomorrow if packing is still behind.”

type.text: Remind me tomorrow if packing is still behind.

steps.say: A standing watch: the server checks packing against its normal range tomorrow and only speaks if it is still behind.
The watch sits with the others until it fires.
And when there is no answer in the data, it says so.

type.text: What revenue did the TrendCart orders bring in this quarter?

steps.say: No prices in the data, so no revenue figure. It never invents one.
ThreadPilot: a manager's co-pilot, all day, with every number traceable.
